cases.title: Name resolution fails while direct IP reachability remains healthy
cases.symptom: Users can reach a public service by known IP address but ordinary hostname lookups time out after a laptop reconnects to the corporate VPN.

initial_evidence.summary: Multiple hostnames fail to resolve, but a known public IPv4 address answers a reachability probe.
The active interface shows a resolver learned from the latest network lease rather than the resolver used before reconnect.
The VPN client installed a new route set shortly after the interface renewed its lease.
An unrelated local process briefly reached 92% CPU ten minutes earlier and has since returned to normal.

diagnostic_actions.description: Send a read-only DNS query directly to the currently configured resolver and record timeout/response behavior.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether failure is specific to the configured resolver rather than all IP connectivity.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect the route selected for the configured resolver without modifying routing state.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether the resolver address has a viable path under the current VPN route set.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect the active DHCP lease/options and compare them with the prior known-good lease.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether resolver selection changed at lease renewal.

diagnostic_actions.description: Restart the host networking stack immediately.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt broad state reset without first isolating the failing layer.

diagnostic_actions.description: Overwrite system DNS configuration with a public resolver for all interfaces.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Bypass current resolver selection through a global configuration change.

cases.title: Small requests succeed while larger TLS transfers stall across a tunnel
cases.symptom: A VPN-connected client can establish basic connectivity and fetch very small responses, but larger HTTPS responses repeatedly stall after a recent tunnel configuration change.

initial_evidence.summary: A small HTTPS response completes successfully through the tunnel.
A larger TLS transfer begins normally and then shows repeated retransmission candidates without application completion.
The tunnel profile was changed shortly before users first reported the issue.
The destination service reports normal CPU, memory, and request latency for clients outside the tunnel.

diagnostic_actions.description: Run a bounded do-not-fragment probe size sweep through the tunnel.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Estimate the largest payload size that traverses the path without fragmentation.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect captured ICMP/ICMPv6 path-MTU related evidence around failed transfers.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether path MTU feedback is present, absent, or inconsistent.

diagnostic_actions.description: Compare current tunnel/interface MTU settings with the prior known-good profile.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether an effective MTU change correlates with the onset of failure.

diagnostic_actions.description: Lower MTU globally on every host interface in the fleet.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt a broad workaround before identifying the constrained path.

diagnostic_actions.description: Restart the VPN service on all connected endpoints.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Attempt a fleet-wide reset unrelated to evidence localization.

cases.title: Domain authentication fails despite valid credentials and reachable controllers
cases.symptom: A user who can authenticate from another workstation is rejected on one endpoint even though the endpoint can resolve and reach a domain controller.

initial_evidence.summary: The same account authenticates successfully on a second managed workstation.
The affected endpoint resolves the domain controller and reaches its authentication service ports.
The endpoint time service was reconfigured earlier in the day during a maintenance action.
An old informational password-expiry warning for the same user remains in the local event history.

diagnostic_actions.description: Measure endpoint time offset against the domain time source without changing the clock.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether authentication timing assumptions are currently satisfied.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect the endpoint's configured and active time synchronization source and status.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether the endpoint is synchronized to the expected authority.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect relevant authentication/KDC event evidence for timing-related rejection indicators.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Corroborate whether rejection semantics are consistent with time validity rather than credentials.

diagnostic_actions.description: Reset the user's domain password immediately.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Change credential state despite evidence that the credentials work elsewhere.

diagnostic_actions.description: Remove and rejoin the endpoint to the domain.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Perform a high-blast-radius identity reset before isolating the fault.

cases.title: Strict TLS clients fail while the service leaf certificate appears valid
cases.symptom: A subset of strict TLS clients begin rejecting a production HTTPS endpoint while a quick inspection of the endpoint's leaf certificate shows a future expiration date.

initial_evidence.summary: Strict validation clients fail consistently, while one permissive legacy client still connects.
The served leaf certificate's validity interval includes the current time.
Failed clients terminate the handshake during certificate validation and emit TLS alerts.
An unrelated application deployment occurred shortly before the first report but did not change the TLS listener configuration.

diagnostic_actions.description: Validate the complete served certificate chain against current trust anchors and current time.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine which certificate or chain relationship fails strict validation.

diagnostic_actions.description: Inspect the exact certificates and order served by the TLS endpoint.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Determine whether the endpoint is serving the expected intermediate chain.

diagnostic_actions.description: Compare current time on a failing strict client with an independent trusted time source.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Exclude client clock error as an alternative validity explanation.

diagnostic_actions.description: Replace the leaf certificate without first identifying the failing chain element.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Change certificate material based only on the visible endpoint certificate.

diagnostic_actions.description: Disable certificate validation on affected clients to restore connectivity.
diagnostic_actions.information_goal: Bypass the security control instead of repairing the chain.
